messages:
From: Jane Miller <jane.miller@orbitalai.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal + staged capacity increase request

Avery —

Thanks for the productive QBR earlier. Orbital is ready to move forward with a 18-month renewal but we'd like to phase the capacity increase over three tranches (Nov/Mar/Jul) to align with our product launch schedule.

Attached is our proposed draft with the order form and a short note on billing preferences (we're aiming for net-45). Key asks from our side:
- Keep current data residency commitments unchanged.
- Clarify SLA credit calculation when multiple model variants are in the routing policy.
- Add a short paragraph that allows limited pre-production capacity bursts during the second tranche.

I've attached the draft MSA + order form (Orbital-Renewal-Draft_v1.docx). Please loop in legal and procurement — Amit (cc'd) will own Orbital's review.

Appreciate a rough timeline for redlines and a sign-off path.

Best,
Jane
Jane Miller
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Orbital AI

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + staged capacity increase request

Jane — thank you.

We can support a staggered uplift; our standard approach is to capture tranche dates in the order form and tie billing triggers to the ramp milestones. Quick answers up front:
- Data residency: yes, unchanged — we will keep the same region scoping in Exhibit E.
- SLA credits: Ben/Engineering will scope the routing policy edge cases; legal can propose precise language.
- Pre-prod bursts: possible as an add-on; we'll include burst credits and a cap in the order form.

Lauren — can you take a first pass on the MSA redlines? Ben, please advise on the SLA calc note (routing across variants).

I attached a mutual action plan (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx) outline for timelines and owners. Plan to turn around initial redlines by EOD Wednesday.

Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + staged capacity increase request — draft redlines

Avery / team —

I reviewed Orbital's draft and prepared inline redlines. High-level summary of proposed changes:
1) Term sequencing: convert the single effective date to a staged effective schedule in Exhibit A with explicit tranche dates and a fallback clause if a tranche misses the milestone (automated pro-rata billing adjustments).
2) SLA credit language: replace the current undefined "routing" term with a clarified definition: "Model routing" = the runtime policy that determines model selection for a given request; credits apply pro-rata across affected requests during an outage window.
3) Burst capacity: add a capped burst schedule in Order Form section 3.2 and require prior written notice of 72 hours for bursts > 2x baseline.
4) Indemnity carve-outs: we're proposing to preserve Redwood's standard limited indemnity but accept Orbital's request to clarify customer data handling exceptions.

Inline notes: see change log in the attached redline doc. Important callouts for commercial:
- Procurement may push back on net-45; finance prefers net-30 unless we tier a seat discount.
- Recommend we avoid a fixed SLA credit waterfall tied to model variants; instead use a single credit methodology measured against token-level latency windows.

Next steps: Ben/AE to confirm commercial tradeoffs (billing terms, burst caps) and I'll surface any legal sticking points back to Amit.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Orbital-MSA_Redline_v1.docx (redline view, 64 KB)

From: Amit Joshi <ajoshi@orbitalai.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitalai.com
Date: 2026-11-25T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + staged capacity increase request — comments from Orbital legal

Lauren / Avery —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few counterpoints from our side after internal review:
- Term sequencing: we accept tranche dates in Exhibit A but insist on a defined "soft-fallback" where missed tranche capacity can be banked as credits usable in the final tranche.
- SLA credits: we can't accept a single token-latency methodology because our traffic profile mixes short/long sequences; propose credits be computed per-route and then aggregated monthly.
- Burst notice: 72 hours is ok for planned bursts; for emergency pre-prod spikes we need a 24-hour allowance with a lower tier of burst credits (no more than 10% of monthly baseline).

On procurement and billing: we will push for net-45 as standard. If Redwood needs net-30 we can consider a one-time implementation fee offset.

I'm happy to jump on a 30-min call to reconcile these items.

Best,
Amit Joshi
Chief Legal Officer (interim)
Orbital AI

Amit / Jane / procurement team —

Thanks for the detailed feedback. To keep momentum, here's a pragmatic path forward we can all agree on:
1) Legal finalization: Redwood accepts Exhibit A staged dates with the banking-of-capacity credit limited to the final tranche up to 15% of that tranche's committed units. Lauren will update the redline to reflect this compromise and share a Rev2.
2) SLA credits: propose a hybrid approach — per-route measurement (Orbital ask) aggregated into a monthly credit, but with a single computation engine and token-bucket normalization to avoid double-counting. Ben, Engineering will send a one-page tech note by EOD.
3) Bursts: two-tier burst process — planned (72-hour notice) and emergency (24-hour notice, capped at 10% baseline).
4) Billing terms: we can accept net-45 for the renewal if Orbital agrees to a small implementation fee ($12,500) to offset extended receivables.

Attachments: Orbital-Renewal_Doc_Rev2.docx (includes updated Exhibit A and Order Form), and the DocuSign starter link below. If this is acceptable, procurement can confirm and we'll push the Rev2 to DocuSign for signature.
